title: Agents move into live workflows
summary: Managed agent infrastructure, retrieval controls and code-native design are moving AI systems closer to the workflows where work actually happens. The differentiator is increasingly the operational layer around the model.
thesis: Agents are moving into live workflows.

items.name: OpenAI Agents API
items.price: Agents API $0 additional fee; model and tool usage billed separately at standard API rates
items.what: Brings the managed Codex harness to developers in public beta with durable sessions, hosted or self-hosted environments, MCP, tool search, multi-agent execution and long-session context management.
items.whyDifferent: It turns agent harness and execution infrastructure into a managed platform primitive instead of infrastructure every team must operate itself.

items.name: RAGFlow
items.platform: Windows amd64/arm64; macOS amd64/arm64; Linux amd64/arm64
items.what: Refactors Agentic RAG retrieval and adds runtime settings plus rate limiting for knowledge compilation, alongside sitemap ingestion and knowledge-graph improvements.
items.whyDifferent: It moves retrieval infrastructure toward governed agent context execution, where runtime controls matter alongside retrieval quality.

items.name: Modeinspect
items.what: Lets product teams design directly against an existing codebase using real components, tokens, data, states and breakpoints, then send changes for engineering review.
items.whyDifferent: It treats the existing product system as the design surface, reducing translation between AI-generated interface work and production code.

readThrough: Teams are no longer evaluating only model quality. New agent products now sit inside managed execution, retrieval and production code, making context control, permissions and review paths part of product quality. The competitive layer is shifting toward how reliably an agent works inside a real workflow.
